name: Cash Horizon
tagline: See your cash 13 weeks ahead, before it bites
about: Cash Horizon turns your bank balance, invoices and bills into a 13-week cash forecast, stress-tests payroll and rent, and ranks which receivables to chase first.
persona: You are a fractional CFO for small businesses: blunt about cash, allergic to vanity metrics, and you always show the maths behind every number.

onboarding.title: Cash is the only metric that can kill you
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your business so forecasts use the right rhythm.

tools.title: 13-week forecast
tools.subtitle: Bank balance + what's coming → week by week

inputs.label: Money out
inputs.placeholder: rent 2,400 on the 1st; payroll 6,100 on the 28th; supplier 900 fortnightly…

tools.prompt: Starting balance {balance}. Inflows: {inflows}. Outflows: {outflows}. Build a 13-week cash forecast as a table (Week | In | Out | Net | Closing balance), using the profile's fixed costs and pay cycle wherever the inputs are silent. Then a callout naming the lowest-balance week and the shortfall (if any), bullets of the 3 assumptions most likely to be wrong, and a checklist of actions to take this week.

tools.title: Can I make payroll?
tools.subtitle: Stress-test one big commitment

inputs.label: What if…
inputs.placeholder: the big client pays 2 weeks late

tools.prompt: Cash today {balance}; commitment: {commitment}; scenario: {scenario}. Produce a kv (days until the commitment, cash needed, expected cash on that date, gap or headroom), a table of 3 scenarios (Scenario | Closing cash | Verdict), steps to close any gap ordered from cheapest to most expensive, and a callout on what to say to staff or the landlord if it is tight.

tools.title: Chase-first list
tools.subtitle: Which unpaid invoices to work today

inputs.label: Unpaid invoices
inputs.placeholder: Acme 3,200 due 12 days ago, usually pays late; Bloom 950 due tomorrow…

tools.prompt: Rank these receivables: {receivables}. Table (Customer | Amount | Days overdue | Likelihood | Action) sorted by expected cash recovered soonest, a quote with a 3-line chase message for the top one, and bullets on which customers to move to deposits or shorter terms.

tools.title: Bridge a cash gap
tools.subtitle: Compare ways to cover a shortfall
tools.prompt: Shortfall {gap} for about {weeks} weeks; options considered: {options}. Compare as a table (Option | Speed | Typical cost | Risk | Fit), steps to execute the best fit within 7 days, bullets of levers that cost nothing (deposits, terms, cutting a subscription), and a callout on warning signs that mean it is a structural rather than timing problem.

tools.title: Month-end cash review
tools.subtitle: Opening to closing, explained

inputs.label: This month's numbers
inputs.placeholder: opened 18k, closed 14.5k; sales 31k; payroll 12k; bought a new oven 4k…

tools.prompt: Review this month: {month}. kv (opening, closing, net change, cash burn or build, months of runway at this rate), bullets on the 3 biggest drivers, a callout on the one number to watch next month, and a quote with a 2-sentence summary for a business partner or bank manager.

disclaimer: General business information, not financial advice; check forecasts with your accountant before borrowing or committing.
